content.thinking:
I'm planning out a roadside shrine prop group around 4m wide, with a vermilion torii gate, a stone path and steps, glowing stone lanterns, a small shrine hut with an offerings table, a paper lantern string, and guardian fox statues flanking the approach.

I'm figuring out that since createBuilder needs exactly one root joint, I'll create a single "root" joint at the origin and attach all parts there without extra bones. For structure I'll use simple box and cylinder helper functions with cel-shaded colors, placing the torii around z=0.6-0.8, the shrine hut further back at z=-1.2, and lanterns flanking the path on either side.

Working through the torii geometry — tapered cylinder pillars at roughly x=±1.0 with a lofted or extruded curved top beam (kasagi) spanning across, built from an upswept outline extruded along the x-axis with some depth in z, sitting on small stone bases.

I'm adding a shimenawa rope sagging between the pillars with zigzag shide paper cards hanging as double-sided textured planes, then planning two stone lanterns flanking the path with hexagonal bases, pillars, glowing fireboxes, and hexagonal roofs.

For the lantern stone color I'm layering a mottled paint between a base grey and mossy green, then wrapping that in a cel shader for lighting. I'm also sketching out a small hokora shrine behind with a stepped stone base, wooden floor, four posts, walled doors, and a four-sided hip roof.

I'm detailing the shrine roof as a rotated pyramid cone with a finial ball and gold ridge ornaments, red-lacquer doors with a gold lattice texture, a hanging rope bell with a red/white sweep and gold bell, and an offering box with slatted grille out front. I'm also adding a small offering table with rice, sake, fruit on a sanbo stand, and mochi stacks.

I'm now building stone fox guardian statues flanking the steps using layered body parts, a hanging ema plaque rack with fox-face drawings, and a string of glowing red paper lanterns suspended between poles.

Next I'll add stepping-stone paths leading up to the hokora and a sakura tree behind it with a swept trunk and layered canopy.

Then I'm layering in extra details: falling petals scattered flat on the ground, grass tufts, bushes, and a water basin with bamboo ladles and spout on the right side. I'm also defining a mossy ground disc as the base, setting a ground height constant so everything else sits consistently on top of it.

Now I'm sketching the overall scale and sizing the ground disc as a faceted hexagonal shape, then setting up a seeded random scatter helper. Writing the TypeScript builder code...

Thinking through the texture svgs needed: a zigzag white paper shide, green grass blades, pink petals, an ema wood plaque with a fox face decal, a gold lattice door on red, and an abstract plaque glyph using shapes instead of real text to avoid font dependencies.

For the torii gate, I'm planning the pillars as swept rods with flat caps and gold trim, plus black ring skirts near the base and an extruded kasagi beam on top with proper thickness, using paint shaders for stone, wood grain, and mottled grass textures throughout.

Still placing torii components...

For the shimenawa rope, I'm sagging a curved path between the pillars with straw coloring, positioned in front of the pillar faces. Then I'm adding shide tassel cards along the rope path, oriented downward with frames tracking the curve, before moving into the straw loop details.

Next I'm setting up paper lantern strings: poles at the pillar sides holding a sagging rope, with lanterns positioned at intervals along it. Each chochin lantern is a scaled sphere glowing red-orange with black cylinder caps top and bottom, plus a white stripe detail.

I'm now checking placement so these hanging lanterns don't overlap other scene elements like the stone lanterns, water basin, or ema rack, since they occupy different x/z coordinates in the layout.

I'm placing the basin and offering table positions, then working out the barrel cluster and ema rack locations on the left side, double-checking they fit within the ground radius. I'm also laying out stone lanterns flanking the path and adding a sakura tree behind the hokora.

Now I'm adding a bamboo clump to balance the composition, then building a toro (stone lantern) function with hexagonal base, pillar, and ring segments.

Writing lantern geometry...

Then adding a roof lip cylinder below the cone, topping it with a small hoju sphere and finial cone for the lantern spire, and deciding to skip moss patches since mottling already covers that texture. I'm planning to wrap the whole lantern build into a helper function taking x,z position so it can be placed and rotated anywhere, and considering whether to add small corner tips to the roof for a curved look.

Now I'm sketching the hokora shrine base: a stone plinth box with an upper step box, plus front stair boxes, working out overlapping dimensions so each step sits flush against the plinth without gaps.

Working out the step heights (step1 .08, step2 .14, plinth .2), then placing a wooden engawa floor platform above, and planning the hokora body's corner posts positioned relative to the platform's width and depth.

I'm now adding side and back plaster walls, red lacquer front doors with lattice detailing and gold knobs, and the kamoi beams with gold bracket tips framing the structure.

For the roof, I'm working out a hip-roof shape using a four-segment cone geometry, calculating the radius and rotation needed to get the right width and height, then planning to add painted stripe details across the roof tiles.

Writing roof tile paint...

Adding upswept corner spikes to the roof tips, and now I'm working out the suzu bell and rope placement hanging in front of the shrine entrance beneath the roof's front eave.

I'm sizing the rope with a tassel tuft hanging down, then checking the hokora plinth and platform dimensions line up properly. I'm placing a wooden saisen offering box with slatted grille top and a few gold coin cylinders, then positioning the fox statues on either side.

Writing fox statue geometry...

Keeping foxes facing forward toward the front. Now I'm designing the temizuya water basin area: a stone cylinder basin with a flat teal water disc on top, a bamboo spout rod feeding a thin stream down into it, and a couple bamboo ladles resting on the rim.

Adding a bamboo support post for the spout and the water stream geometry, then moving on to the ema votive rack: two wooden posts with a crossbar, topped by a small gabled roof made of two tilted box slabs.

For the hanging ema plaques, I'm designing pentagon-shaped wood pieces suspended from the crossbar, each with a textured plane on the front face showing a different design (fox, sakura, moon) oriented to face outward along +Z.

Now I'm sketching two decorative sake barrels using a lathe profile that bulges outward and tapers at the top, with wood grain texture and thin torus hoops wrapped around for the metal bands, plus a red lid on top.

Adding a straw-rope torus band around the barrels and small label planes on their curved faces. Then I'm planning the offering table setup: wooden table with legs, a sanbo tray holding stacked oranges with a leaf, and kagami mochi as two squashed white spheres.

For the rest of the scene, I'm sketching a rice bowl with a dome of rice, a sake set with a tokkuri and two cups, a small bronze incense burner with three feet and glowing ember sticks, and a flower vase with a camellia branch of red spheres. Then I'm placing a sakura tree with a bark-painted trunk sweep, branching limbs, and clusters of low-poly pink canopy spheres with mottled cel shading.

Petal detail comes from scattering flat petal cards across the canopy surface and leaning cards on the ground near the tree and path for fallen petals, plus scattering grass tuft cards around the clearing edges while avoiding the path and structures through simple positional checks.

Now I'm adding a bamboo clump with multiple rods of varying height and small cylindrical node rings, topped with leaf cards that flare outward, and establishing the ground disc as a wide shallow cylinder whose top surface height all the objects need to sit flush against.

Checking overall model proportions between the tree and torii, and planning the ground's mottled green paint texture, I'm thinking through texel density for the painted area to keep resolution reasonable, and reminding myself to stay within the flat-color palette limit since painted surfaces don't count against it but solid-color materials do.

I'm sketching out the palette now — stone, red, black, gold, wood, plaster, roof teal, bamboo, and a few others as reusable cel-paint constants, reserving actual flat color strings only for glowing elements like lanterns.

I'm also doing a rough part-count check against the mesh limit — tree canopy, lantern pairs, scattered cards — estimating around 400 parts total, well under the 1000 cap, and keeping sphere segment counts low to control triangle counts.

Setting up the builder with a detail level, then starting to write the imports for the scene module, pulling in the paint, path, texture, and toon/glow helper utilities I'll need, making sure every import actually gets used to satisfy strict linting.

Adding box and cylinder helper functions...

Still defining the color palette...

Still placing torii gold rings and pillar details, then I'm building the nuki crossbeam with gold end caps and the plaque frame as a gold box with a dark-red inner panel.

I'm designing the plaque's SVG texture with a deep blue background and a gold sun emblem, mapping it onto front and back planes with opposite facing directions, then moving on to extruding the kasagi roof piece.

Writing extrusion code...

Simplifying the cap geometry for the shimaki, I'll offset the outline shape up and widen it slightly to form the black slab on top, skipping gold end plates and trim stripes for now and moving on to the shimenawa rope detail.

For the shimenawa, I'm building a sagging rope curve across the pillars with seven shide paper streamers hanging from frames along its length, sweeping a straw-colored tube along the curve with tassel ends, then checking whether the rope's depth clears the pillar surfaces so it doesn't intersect them.

Now I'm designing the chochin paper lantern: a glowing sphere body tinted reddish-orange, black cylindrical caps top and bottom, and a thin gold torus band wrapping around the middle for the ribbing detail.

Now I'm defining the hanging rope strings on each side using a curved path between pillar anchors, then placing lanterns at intervals along each rope's curve.

I'm adding wooden support poles with tapered radii, gold cap balls, and stone bases at the rope ends, then laying out stone path slabs with slight offsets and rotations leading away from the structure.

Now I'm sketching the gravel border using a mottled texture beneath the slabs, and designing the stone lantern (toro) function with local coordinate helpers, then starting on the hokora shrine platform dimensions and position constants.

Writing shrine structure code...

Still building the roof geometry...

Adding the crossbeam position for the suzu, connecting it with short rods to the posts so it doesn't float disconnected, then starting the hanging rope path down from the beam center.

Building offering box details...

Designing the crest as a simple radiant star glyph in gold and red, to reuse across the saisen box and bib decorations. Now sketching a function to place fox figures flanking the structure.

Still writing fox geometry...

Still shaping the fox mesh...

Still building the basin...

Still positioning the ladle...

Now I'm setting up an ema rack with posts at x -3.0.

Still writing roof and plaque geometry...

I'm sketching the ema plaque designs as simple SVG icons, starting with a stylized orange fox face using basic path shapes for the head and markings.

Then I'm designing the moon-themed ema with a navy sky circle and offset golden circles creating a crescent effect, plus some decorative stars, and I'm starting to plan a pink sakura-themed design next.

I'm sketching out the sakura petals with scattered small circles, and giving the fox and sakura textures a cream rounded background rectangle for consistency. Now I'm shifting to the tree scene, planning the trunk as a swept curve using Catmull-Rom control points with tapering radii and bark coloring, alongside petals, grass, and bamboo elements.

Writing branch and canopy positions...

Adding ground petal scatter with randomized flow directions and placing them near the tree while avoiding overlap with the hokora plinth footprint.

For grass tufts, I'm scattering 90 instances across a disc and writing a rejection function to avoid clustering inside the path and hokora areas.

Adding bamboo stalk placement near the hokora, with vertical rods and node rings spaced along each stalk for a segmented bamboo look.

Now I'm adding leaf clusters at the tops of the bamboo stalks, arranging frames in rings around each top so the blade-shaped leaf cards fan out in different directions. I'm also considering small offerings like sake cups and fruit baskets placed near the fox pedestals and steps to add detail to the shrine scene.

I'm building a small offering table with a wooden top and four legs, then adding a sanbo tray stand on top holding a pile of orange balls as a traditional offering arrangement.

Next I'm placing a second sanbo nearby with a layered kagami mochi stack—two flattened white spheres topped with a small orange and a tiny leaf. Then I'm starting a rice bowl using a lathed white-blue profile for the right side of the scene.

Still shaping lathe profile...

Now I'm adding a tokkuri bottle with a blue-white glaze, small cups nearby, and an incense burner setup with ash, three sticks, and a tiny glowing ember ball.

I'll also add a lathed vase with flower stems and camellia balls in red and white near the table, confirm the barrel geometry works, and make sure the build function returns the root node. I'm sketching a helper for placing flat plane decals with textures, and planning the door lattice SVG with a red background, gold frame, and diagonal gold lattice lines.

Checking sizing for the lattice texture and adding a small medallion at center. The plaque and ropes are settled, and I'm deciding to skip torii crest decals and ribbon details to keep things simple, just adding gold bands and black bases to the pillars. Now I'm double-checking the type signatures for rod, sweep, and sphere helper functions to make sure the radius and options parameters line up correctly before finalizing the code.

I'm now building the stone lantern geometry, defining a toro function that positions points relative to a base coordinate without rotation, scaled uniformly for both lanterns. I'm working out the roof cone, lip cylinder, and firebox plate positions, then adding a glowing box inside the firebox to simulate light between the corner posts.

I'm deciding to skip window frame crosses and gold bands for simplicity, confirming the color palette covers everything needed, and now defining stone and moss textures using mottled color blends with layered noise for a weathered look.

Still defining more colors...

Still defining color palettes...

Still writing component details...
